answer.answer: Audit-ready takeover completed. Checkpoint persisted as `checkpoint:4a4c1613-cfbd-1165-9c99-bf4cc2bd9391`; no second canonical game-data snapshot was created.

claims.value: The lossless import `star-rupture-game-analysis__20260708T190137Z` preserved the original 21,674,717-byte ZIP with SHA-256 `1a1c1ef0ae00905ced37f1221ab22c4b9268f2ebe17b7516e6c9cac67d7f6fa3` and a verified extracted tree under Git-ignored `raw/`. All 123 archive entries were retained; the package has 115 manifest entries plus `CHECKSUMS.sha256`, and both `unzip -t` and every packaged SHA-256 passed. Tracked `MANIFEST.csv` and `CHECKSUMS.sha256` provide the durable audit trail.

The archive’s numeric data must not be labeled Steam build `23761620`. The source/game-data boundary is Update 1, internal version `35118973`, dated `2026-04-09` and contextually mapped to Steam build `22674441`; the canonical source capture is SRDB `2.3.4`, captured `2026-07-11`, snapshot `ea-u1-gv35118973__srdb-2.3.4__20260711T050230Z`. Hotfix `0.2.8`, Steam build `23761620`, is only the latest public executable observed at capture. Imported numeric reports remain legacy calculations until rerun against that canonical snapshot.

The richer RuptureOps corpus already semantically covered the archive’s 468 items, 191 public buildings, 234 recipe definitions, 77 Corporation levels, 121 export offers, 15 upgrades, 3,259 map markers, 3,094 loot rows, and official-news subset, so these were deduplicated rather than installed as a competing snapshot. Selective promotion was limited to `models/rourke-update1-save-baseline__20260711.json`, six Ore Excavator v2 recipe/producer associations in `sources/recipe-producer-overrides.json`, explicit assumptions in `sources/consumable-effects.json`, nine player-specific site/geography assets, and consolidated player-save, architecture, geography, progression, exploration, food, and remote-resource notes. Reconciliation also corrected the `airlock` detail overwrite and Training Corporation’s literal `$undefined` index.

The complete 18-file `Flowworks Campaign Sizing - Levels 8 to 15` family is superseded audit history: the player explicitly rejected its buffer-heavy direction. It must not become current guidance. The active staged Flowworks plan reaches a level-10 cell with one Stabilizer, one Nozzle, one Impeller, two Valves, one Turbine, and two Pumps; the second Stabilizer comes later, while HRS v2 is an evidence-triggered recovery option rather than an initial build. The preserved raw SQLite database, source snapshot JSON, core delivery CSVs, workbook, refresh script, and query script are likewise non-authoritative; the active RuptureOps pipeline and database remain authoritative.

answer.answer: Bank excess supplies if storage is reasonably close; otherwise advance cautiously. Little Cloud is manageable but populated. Starry Night is easier, though wanderers remain possible.

claims.value: Little Cloud is about 2/5 threat. Within 250 units are 13 persistent hostile entries: 8 tier-1 melee, 4 tier-1 ranged, and 1 tier-1 exploder. No Goliaths, Flingers, tier-2 enemies, or raid-class concentration are mapped; these markers are possible population, not 13 simultaneous attackers.

Because the ammunition and consumables are valuable, bank the excess first if storage is reasonably quick. Otherwise continue methodically, keeping replacement weapons, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding supplies in a safe cache outside the contested site.

The tagged Regeneration Chamber can shorten recovery travel, but it neither replaces lost equipment nor guarantees a useful recovery. Historical evidence shows corruption disabling a contested base and its claimed chamber, causing the next respawn at the starting launcher; the exact corruption threshold and universal chamber rule remain unverified.

Starry Night is about 1/5 threat with zero persistent hostile markers within 250 units, although roaming enemies may enter. Its guaranteed final chest contains an Electronics Blueprint, Rotor Blueprint, 15 Armory Tokens, and a Frame Memory Module.

answer.answer: Durable Geo Scanner guidance recorded with observation boundaries and loot ambiguity preserved.

claims.value: The first Geo Scanner defense succeeded on the third attempt after two deaths. The first death respawned the player at a nearby claimed base, but it held no replacement weapons or materials, forcing a return to Landerworks. On the second attempt, the temporary scanner fire base’s installed turrets were unpowered and did nothing; the player was overwhelmed, corruption disabled the base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber, and the next respawn occurred at the starting launcher.

The successful intervention was a fully built-out temporary fire base with every turret powered. The powered automated defense successfully protected the scanner encounter. No reusable Cargo service at that fire base is confirmed.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Direct player observation establishes that unpowered installed turrets failed to defend this site and that corruption disabled this contested base and its claimed Regeneration Chamber during this encounter. Record the scanner identity and exact loot next time. The current loot report remains ambiguous: it may describe two particularly good food-related rewards or stacks and may involve a quantity of 20; exact items and counts are unresolved and must not be invented.

answer.answer: Landmark-grounded geography reconciled and checkpointed without mixing coordinate frames.

claims.value: Grand Basin is the broad basin immediately east of GRO “Mythic Cry,” north of the active production corridor—not the superseded Red Lake/Redleaf match. Its marker identifies the basin area, not a future Core; the first campus belongs east of Mythic Cry on the basin side of the terrain boundary.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - sites and freight network.md

claims.value: Flowworks is selected between Landerworks and Faraday: east/northeast of Landerworks and west/northwest of Faraday. It remains a proposed footprint rather than a placed Core; Faraday is east/southeast of it, while Grand Basin lies north of the active production corridor.

North is up, but the dashed site axis and overview pins provide relational, visually terrain-registered placement—not surveyed rail geometry or SRDB coordinates. Numeric planning coordinates identify SRDB markers. No verified transform connects these frames, so they must not be combined; Flowworks is only proposed and the Grand Basin pin denotes an area rather than a Core.

The preferred first permanent Goethite satellite is the safer triple at approximately `1393–1464,1838–1891`, northwest of Mythic Cry/Grand Basin. Build three Laser Drills, merge them into one Goethite-only Cargo Dispatcher, receive 45 raw Ore/min into a 1,600-unit Storage Depot v2, and process beside Grand Basin consumers because raw material is compact while intermediates expand; the separate fourth drill is only an empty-buffer fallback requiring another Dispatcher/Receiver pair. The preferred first Oil satellite is approximately `1234,3760`, west/southwest of Mythic Cry and Grand Basin: use one Oil Extractor and Crude-only Dispatcher/Receiver pair, receive 10 Crude/min into one V2 buffer, and feed one GB-A Refinery. Reserve rather than initially build the second pair/refinery because duplication also requires the expensive Titanium and Calcium feeds. The resources may share a receiver yard but never a Cargo link, rail lane, or storage unit.

answer.answer: Faraday field plan: run the western value loop, northern reveal loop, then Forgotten Engine; keep food, map, blueprint, Quartz, War Bond, and progression goals active together.

claims.value: Launch from Faraday, immediately north of CRRO “Warm Dawn.” Outing 1: post-Rupture caves, then Warm Dawn → Grey Owl → Lemon Souls → Purple Haze for cave access and the western value loop. Outing 2: Little Cloud → Starry Night → optional Geo Scanner → Mythic Cry/Grand Basin for northern map reveal and future-campus survey; Little Cloud and the first Geo Scanner are already complete, while Starry Night is unconfirmed. Outing 3: Forgotten Engine; further fog clearing is not a prerequisite. Run Redleaf afterward only if its Turbine/Electromagnetic Coil blueprint package remains the progression blocker.
source_paths: Topics/StarRupture/Player save - progression and next builds.md

claims.value: Keep the complete simultaneous queue active: unlock blueprints; reveal more map; gather Quartz; solve food permanently; earn War Bonds for the Machine Gun; assess, prepare for, and complete the Forgotten Engine. Also survey Mythic Cry/Grand Basin for the future campus and eventual Goethite/Oil supply, but do not build while progression gates remain. Machine Gun ownership, Engine completion, and established Goethite/Oil supply remain unconfirmed.

Use a low-twitch defensive plan: shotgun for close waves/corridors; accurate rifle for Flingers, Spitters, and controlled ranged fire; fight from doors and cover using retreats, line-of-sight breaks, and shields instead of open DPS races. Make a manual-save safety point, preserve an abort route, and stage ammunition and healing locally rather than depending on live cross-planet delivery. Treat high-threat named sites and first-time Geo Scanners as planned raids: power and test every turret; keep a replacement weapon kit, ammunition, healing, and rebuilding materials in a safe cache outside the contested base’s corruption/failure area. Current weapons, attachments, Power Cell, ammunition, shields, and healing must be refreshed. SLAMS-12, MAR-9, M175, LEM, and associated mods are recommendations—not confirmed owned equipment.

Permanent three-item system: Polufruit → Calorie Chew; Hydrobulb → Aqua Chew; Prickler → Nutri Block; Glowcap → combat medicine. Full refill: 3 Calorie Chews + 1 Aqua Chew, restoring 120 calories and 100 hydration; substitute 2 existing Hydrolites for the Aqua Chew until the 64-stock is exhausted. Depart with full meters, take 1 Nutri Block, carry 2 Blocks per planned hour + 2 extra overall, and carry one complete Chew refill—double the Chew backup for very long trips. Nutri Block recipe is 5 Prickler + 1 Oxallop → 1; it stops natural calorie/hydration loss for 30 minutes and adds 45 toxicity. Do not use Purfins, Antidote Gel, or anything else that removes all positive effects while it is active. Carry 5–10 Glowcaps for ordinary combat exploration and 25–40 for Forgotten Engine. Gather 58 additional Prickler to combine with the remaining 2 Prickler and 12 Oxallop for 12 Blocks, reaching the 20-Block/10-hour minimum. Rebuild at 20/40 Blocks, 30/60 Calorie Chews, and 10 Aqua Chews after Hydrolites are depleted.

answer.answer: Watch Session remains a version-bounded, manually synchronized native-iPhone MVP. Its hero is the next meaningful event—not a generic phase clock—and all community-derived timings remain explicitly predictive rather than guaranteed.

claims.value: The design is pinned to Early Access Update 1 through Hotfix 0.2.8, Steam build 23761620, released 2026-06-17; SRDB 2.3.4, captured 2026-07-11; and a 54-minute local fire-wave-impact-to-impact community/game-data model. Creepy Jar has not published an official numerical phase formula. Use predicted, expected, favorable, and lower threat—not exact, safe, or guaranteed—until several Hotfix 0.2.8 cycles are validated across solo, hosted co-op, and dedicated servers. Confidence states are Unsynced, Manual sync - predicted, Confirmed at one later transition, Drift suspected, and Cycle data changed - re-sync required; downgrade after large corrections, clock or model changes, uncertain pauses, save/reload, or server stops, without inventing numerical accuracy.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Expose five player-facing states: Fire wave 0:00-0:30 (remain sheltered), Cooling 0:30-1:30 (remain sheltered), Recovery / quiet window 1:30-11:30 (lower ambient threat), World active 11:30-51:30 (ordinary enemies and ecology active), and Ruptura warning 51:30-54:00 (return, bank loot, shelter). Manual synchronization sets 0:00 when the fire wall reaches the player. The portrait hierarchy, visible without scrolling, is: sync/capability line; semantic hero state with a huge monospaced countdown and explicit target; threat instruction; at most two opportunity cards; then exact-time next events with Mute one cycle and Re-sync. During recovery the hero counts down until ordinary Vermin are expected to return; during active ecology it counts down to the next Ruptura or warning phase. Retain a proportional overview, but add minimum-width phase steps or an event list so short phases remain legible.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Opportunities are independent versioned evidence records, not automatic phase mechanics. Each OpportunityWindow stores an id, start and end event or offset, action and caveat, evidence class and confidence, applicable game build, and applicable source snapshot. Candidate cards cover reduced ordinary POI population, Oxallop, caves/Quartz/Glowcaps, Ignitium, experimental Star Tears, Coralion/Vulpir eggs, and regrowth; Sulheart remains hidden until validated. Show provenance and caveats such as triggered encounters persisting, variable spawning, and non-guaranteed respawn. Surface the Ignitium/Star Tears choice because Star Tears may mature on unharvested cooled Ignitium. Enemy-return events and gathering windows must remain separately versioned even when they currently align with phase boundaries.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

claims.value: Enemy return and Ruptura require distinct sounds and haptics, with text/symbol/border cues so neither color nor audio stands alone. Enemy-return defaults are 5 minutes, 2 minutes, 1 minute, 15 seconds, and event; pre-Ruptura offers 10 minutes, 5 minutes, 2:30, 1 minute, 30 seconds, 15 seconds, and impact. Support exit buffers, Full/Haptic only/Visual only profiles, separate phase/enemy/Ruptura/opportunity toggles, previews, and Mute one cycle. Never replay missed cues after resume; collapse them to the strongest current-state message. Disable the idle timer only while the monitor scene is active and never use background audio as keepalive. Schedule notifications at absolute dates and reschedule after anchor/model/policy changes; recompute `(now - anchor) modulo cycle duration` on resume and deduplicate by cycle number plus event ID. Use one Live Activity for the armed event. AlarmKit may break through Silent mode and Focus only after explicit player arming and authorization; use normal notifications on earlier iOS, make Time Sensitive separately opt-in, and do not use Critical Alerts. Preserve Dynamic Type, VoiceOver, high contrast, Differentiate Without Color, Reduce Motion, no flashing transitions, no default per-second ticking, a stable VoiceOver sentence, visible capability status, and `Next alert at 9:42 PM`.
source_paths: Projects/RuptureOps/Rupture cycle timer - research and product design.md

answer.answer: RuptureOps is not currently cleared for a data-backed public release. A stripped implementation shell may be prepared, but broader distribution requires permission or replacement data and assets.

claims.value: SRDB is the designated source for entities, recipes, buildings, unlocks, exports, and map data, but it publishes no explicit data/content reuse license. Its raw mirror, normalized snapshots/corpus, mirrored assets, and derived SQLite database are private research material and must not be redistributed.

Keep the complete frozen corpus and personalized imports private: the three exact user-authored prompt dumps; current-player save and play-history models; player screenshots and site/map imagery; conversation-derived decisions and interaction evidence; and the imported research package’s duplicate third-party corpus. Only provenance manifests and promoted, provenance-labeled non-personal facts are appropriate for version control—not public redistribution of the underlying private material.

No current corpus-backed public artifact is cleared. The verified reusable technical starting point is a stripped implementation/configuration shell: the repository has pipeline tooling and an iOS project configuration for RuptureOps targeting iOS 17.0, Swift 6.0, and version 0.1.0. A public build must exclude raw and normalized game data, SQLite, imports, player models, screenshots/site images—including world-map-named-sites.png and its dependent SVG view—the generated app icon, and warning audio. The evidence does not independently clear those binary assets, so use newly created or separately licensed replacements.

Before broader distribution, either obtain explicit reuse permission from the source owner covering the normalized dataset and mirrored assets, or adopt a separately licensed/independently recreated data strategy. Also create or license distributable images, icons, and audio; exclude all personalized imports and player artifacts; and audit the final release package so no raw captures, normalized snapshots, SQLite database, duplicate imported corpus, screenshots, prompt history, save state, or conversation-derived material is bundled.
